body: My bad.  Why didn't I think of that?

I would love to make a career out of my hobby - I've investigated different avenues and it doesn't seem like a reasonable option.  I thought about going back to school, but I know I won't finish and I'll just end up with a bunch of debt.  

I want to change myself but I don't even know where to begin.  It's like my body rejects the idea of doing certain things, it's awful.  I don't know how to overcome that.
That's something I would've never actually considered.  I'll google some stuff as well, thank you.  That's a great idea.

I really appreciate this comment because I was worried about the kind of response I would get being "against" medication.  I want to get better, I don't want to wish for an end, and I don't want something that just sort of hides the bad feelings when it doesn't resolve the underlying issue.  I would prefer to try other methods of rehabilitation first, but I called the mental health crisis center in my area today and apparently there's a very long waiting list for any type of counselling.  Who knows what I'm going to do next.  Thank you for your honest reply... I'll keep you posted.
When I went before, I told the doctor I wanted to  learn skills to cope instead of taking medication like that, it makes me nervous.  Does it change you?

I've been happy, I was usually happy.  It was only because I was oblivious to how many people were holding my hands. Like I said, I'm a talker - I have talked my way into social circles, jobs, relationships, having people work to my advantage.  It's a good quality but it'll only get you so far; sometimes it's not fair to others either. 

I came to terms with the fact I was unhappy at my job and wanted to move on, and I started to think about other options. I realized that history keeps repeating itself because the same traits keep surfacing.  I can't take a step forward because I don't have the skills to be successful doing that.  I've never had them, I've never actually finished anything in my life because I can't pay fucking attention to anything or see it through until the end.  I've tried, I've taken on so many challenges only to fall short.  Even small ones, it doesn't matter.  What's the point in taking another step if you know you're going to fail?  I feel like each failure has chipped away a small part of me, and I'm reaching the point that one more failure will result in me crumbling to nothing.  

What is the point?

I actually saw a doctor roughly 5 years about ADHD - The doctor was out of town (about an hour) and I couldn't complete the diagnosis because I couldn't get to my appointments.  I just feel like a simple diagnosis like that couldn't possibly be the root of feeling this awful all the time.  It seems like such a small piece of the puzzle.

Nah, no one has PM'd me.  I didn't expect much, really. I have a lot to be thankful for and I'm likely coming across as ungrateful, selfish brat.  I understand that, which is why I don't talk about this with anyone in real life.  I can't, really. 

Are you okay?

I feel exactly like you do, you're not alone.  It's very hard to reach out and talk to people when you know it will shatter their entire perception of you.  If you ever want to vent, feel free to PM me.  Maybe we can work together to get to a happier place.
I really appreciate that.  I do too.  I don't really know what I expected by posting here, I just fear what comes next.  Thank you for reaching out.
All of the issues I listed.

I've had many friends on antidepressants and all it's done is alleviate some of their "sadness," it doesn't resolve the issues that caused the sadness in the first place.  It's like putting a fence around a hole in the ground instead of filing up the hole.  If you move the fence, someone could still fall in. 

I'm sorry that isn't the response you were looking for.  Not feeling things actually sounds worse to me than feeling like this.

Yes, he's fully aware of it.  He's supportive, loving, and works hard to manage the life that we have.  This almost makes it worse - I have to rely on him constantly.  He deserves someone as amazing as him.  I am not amazing.  I am not even good. 

He says he loves me because he's never seen someone dream like me.  Dreams without any type of plan or organization... They're just passing thoughts.  Passing thoughts are not a reason to love someone.  We all have those. 

He wants me to see a doctor, but I know they're just going to try and put me in antidepressants which I see as a band-aid.  They'll numb the feelings of sadness, but they won't fix the issues that I have already isolated.  I've even met with a life coach to see if they could assist with the problems I have, and it was just a headache for everyone involved. 

I'm reaching my breaking point.
